notes.sowing: Plant cloves pointed end up, {cm:5} to {cm:7.5} deep, from about 3 weeks before to 1 week after your first fall frost, so roots grow before the ground freezes. Use the largest cloves of a variety suited to your climate. Spring planting works but gives small bulbs.
notes.care: Most varieties need 1 to 2 months below {c:10} to form bulbs; in frost-free climates, chill cloves in the refrigerator before planting. Mulch over winter where the ground freezes. Cut hardneck flower stems once they curl, and stop watering as the leaves yellow.
notes.harvest: Lift when the lower leaves are brown and about half the upper ones are still green. Cure in a dry, airy, shady place for 2 to 4 weeks, then trim the tops.
